config.title: Conditional Classes

intro.title: Conditional Classes
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple toggle button that changes its appearance based on its state. You will learn how to dynamically apply CSS classes in Vue using the `:class` binding. The core concept is conditional rendering of styles, where a class is added or removed based on a reactive data property. This involves using Vue's reactivity system and a computed property or inline expression to control the class. By the end, you'll understand how to make your UI elements respond visually to user interactions.
intro.usecase: Conditional classes are essential for creating responsive, interactive interfaces that provide clear visual feedback to users. In real-world Vue applications, you'll use them to highlight active navigation items in menus, indicate form validation states (like showing red borders on invalid fields), and toggle UI states in dashboards and admin panels. For example, an e-commerce site might use conditional classes to mark selected product filters or indicate low inventory items, while a project management tool could highlight overdue tasks or completed items. This pattern allows developers to create dynamic, professional interfaces that respond to user interactions and application state changes.

objectives: Apply conditional class binding to dynamically style Vue components based on state
Construct multiple class bindings using both object and array syntax in Vue templates
Implement computed properties to manage complex conditional class logic
Configure class bindings that respond to user interactions and data changes
Integrate conditional classes with component props to create reusable styled components
Manipulate class bindings to create visual feedback for application state changes

steps.title: Import Vue and ref
steps.instruction: Import Vue and ref from 'vue' to enable reactive state in the component.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the necessary Vue APIs.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing from a module
import { ref } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have access to Vue's reactivity system through the ref function.
successCriteria: Vue and ref are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import both Vue and ref from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. Please import Vue and ref from 'vue'.

steps.title: Create main Vue component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named 'ConditionalClassDemo' that uses the Composition API setup function and returns a template with a root div element.
steps.hint: Define a component with the setup function and return a template structure. The root element should be a div.
steps.seedCode:
import { ref } from 'vue'

// Create your ConditionalClassDemo component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A Vue component named ConditionalClassDemo is defined with a setup function that returns a template containing a root div element.
successCriteria: The component is named ConditionalClassDemo, uses the setup function, and returns a template with a root div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your component is named ConditionalClassDemo, uses the setup function, and returns a template with a root div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a Vue component named ConditionalClassDemo with a setup function that returns a template containing a root div element.

steps.title: Initialize reactive state for active state
steps.instruction: Inside your ConditionalClassDemo component, use the imported ref function to create a reactive boolean state variable named isActive with an initial value of false.
steps.hint: Remember that ref() creates reactive state. Pass false as the argument to set the initial value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating reactive state for a toggle
const isVisible = ref(false)
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have a reactive isActive state variable initialized to false, ready to track whether an element should have an active class.
successCriteria: The component contains a reactive isActive state variable created with ref(false)
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using ref() to create reactive state and naming the variable exactly 'isActive' with initial value false.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside the setup function, use ref(false) to create a reactive state variable named isActive.

steps.title: Define toggle handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, define a function named toggleActive that toggles the value of isActive between true and false.
steps.hint: You can toggle a boolean value by setting it to the opposite of its current value using the logical NOT operator (!).
steps.expectedOutcome: A toggleActive function is defined that correctly toggles the isActive state value.
successCriteria: The toggleActive function is defined inside setup() and toggles isActive.value using the logical NOT operator.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it correctly toggles the isActive value using the logical NOT operator (!).
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggle handler function is not defined correctly. Remember to create a function that toggles the isActive value between true and false.

steps.title: Add container div to template
steps.instruction: In the ConditionalClassDemo component's setup function, return a template that includes a div element as the main container.
steps.hint: Remember that in Vue's setup function, you return an object that includes the template. The template can be a simple string containing HTML.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a basic template structure with a div container.
successCriteria: The setup function returns an object with a template property containing a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning the template from the setup function. The template should be a string containing a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: In the setup function, you need to return an object that includes a template property with a div element as a string.

steps.title: Add element with conditional class binding
steps.instruction: Inside the template's container div, add a div element with a :class binding that applies the 'active' CSS class when isActive is true.
steps.hint: Use Vue's class binding syntax: :class="{ 'active': isActive }". This will add the 'active' class to the div only when isActive is true.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now contains a div element with a conditional class binding that will apply the 'active' class based on the isActive state.
successCriteria: A div element with :class binding is added to the template, using the syntax :class="{ 'active': isActive }".
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a div element, but the conditional class binding might be incomplete. Make sure you're using :class="{ 'active': isActive }" syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The conditional class binding wasn't added correctly. You need to add a div element with :class binding that applies the 'active' class based on isActive.

steps.title: Add text content to demonstrate class state
steps.instruction: Inside the div with the conditional class binding, add a paragraph element that displays text indicating whether the element is active or inactive based on the isActive state.
steps.hint: Use the isActive reactive value to conditionally display different text. You can use a ternary operator or a computed property in the template.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: displaying state-based text

{{ isActive ? 'Element is active!' : 'Element is inactive.' }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will display text that changes based on the isActive state, showing 'Element is active!' when isActive is true and 'Element is inactive.' when false.
successCriteria: A paragraph element is added inside the div with conditional class binding that displays text reflecting the current isActive state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a paragraph, but it doesn't yet reflect the isActive state. Make sure to use isActive to conditionally display different text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph isn't displaying text based on the isActive state. Try using a ternary operator with isActive to show different messages.

steps.title: Add toggle button and wire click event
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside the template's container div, with the text 'Toggle Active State', and wire its @click event to call the toggleActive function.
steps.hint: Use the @click directive to bind the button's click event to your toggleActive function. The button should be a sibling to the existing div with the conditional class.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click handler in Vue template
<button @click="handleClick">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Toggle Active State' appears below the colored box, and clicking it toggles the active class on the box.
successCriteria: Button element with text 'Toggle Active State' is present in the template
Button has @click event handler that calls toggleActive function
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but it might be missing the @click binding or the correct function call. Make sure to wire the click event properly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button element or its click handler is not correctly implemented. Check that you've added the button with the proper @click directive.

steps.title: Add button text indicating its purpose
steps.instruction: Inside the button element in your template, add text content that clearly indicates it toggles the active state (e.g., 'Toggle Active State').
steps.hint: Add descriptive text between the button's opening and closing tags to explain what the button does.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: adding descriptive button text
<button @click="handleClick">Click to Toggle</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The button will display clear text indicating its purpose to toggle the active state.
successCriteria: Button contains descriptive text content (e.g., 'Toggle Active State' or similar) between its opening and closing tags.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some text, but make sure it clearly indicates the button toggles the active state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button still lacks descriptive text. Add text between the button tags that explains what the button does.

steps.title: Add CSS styles for visual feedback
steps.instruction: Add a style section with CSS rules for the active class to provide visual feedback when the element is toggled.
steps.hint: Add a <style> tag after the template section and define CSS rules for the .active class.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a style section with CSS rules that visually demonstrate the effect of the conditional class binding.
successCriteria: A style section is added with at least one CSS rule for the .active class.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a style section, but make sure it includes CSS rules for the .active class to demonstrate the conditional class effect.
steps.feedbackWrong: The style section is missing or doesn't contain CSS rules for the .active class. Add a <style> tag with rules that will visually indicate when the element is active.
